novelty.justification: The claim’s proposed novelty is a broader setting plus an alternative measurement: “the tracing-editing dissociation—documented for single models—holds systematically across model families and relations,” while a “direct edit-efficacy probe” estimates layer leverage. Searches for “causal tracing predict best editing layer,” “localization inform editing gradient layer selection,” and “edit efficacy probe knowledge editing” identify Hase et al., Does Localization Inform Editing? (NeurIPS 2023), as the closest work: it already finds that causal-tracing localization does not predict the best MLP layer to edit, while later layer-selection and attribution-based editing work makes gradient-based selection a familiar approach. Extending that established dissociation across models, relations, and editing methods is a natural extension, and the underspecified forward-backward leverage probe appears to apply standard gradient attribution rather than introduce a new core measurement principle.
